title: K-th Smallest Pair Distance
statement: A field crew has placed sensors along a straight pipeline; nums[i] is the position of sensor i (positions may repeat, and the list is not sorted). The gap between two sensors i and j is the absolute difference |nums[i] - nums[j]|. Considering every unordered pair i < j exactly once, list all gaps in non-decreasing order and return the k-th value in that list (k is 1-indexed). If the array has fewer than 2 sensors, or k exceeds the total number of pairs n*(n-1)/2, return -1. Constraints: n up to 10^4 and positions up to 10^6, so enumerating and sorting all O(n^2) gaps is too slow -- binary search the gap value itself, using a two-pointer count of pairs within a given gap as the predicate.
hints: You can't afford all O(n^2) gaps -- but for a fixed distance d, could you count in O(n) how many pairs have a gap of at most d, and is that count monotonic in d?

Sort the array, then binary search d over [0, max - min]. Count pairs with gap <= d using a two-pointer sweep: for each right index, advance left while a[right] - a[left] > d and add (right - left) to the count.

Find the FIRST d where pairs_leq(d) >= k: while lo < hi, if the count at mid is >= k set hi = mid, else lo = mid + 1. Do not return mid the moment the count equals k -- a whole interval of d values can share that count, and only the boundary lo is guaranteed to be an actual pair distance.
